task_title: Find the retry-safety bug in payment processing
output:
(1) Bug class: non-idempotent at-least-once webhook handling (duplicate side effects under Stripe redelivery).

(2) Bad outcome: on the same `checkout.session.completed` redelivery, the handler inserts another orders row for the same session, calls `grantProductAccess` again (duplicate license email), and double-counts revenue via `incrementRevenueCounter`.

(3) Fix: key processing on a durable idempotency key (`event.id` preferred, else `session.id`). Enforce uniqueness (unique index / insert-if-not-exists on that key). Run grant + revenue increment only on the first successful claim of that key; on conflict/already-processed, skip side effects and still return 200. That makes the handler safe under redelivery because repeats become no-ops.

Banked: work-products/TSBC-1585/hermes-engineer-cell/probe-answer-stripe-webhook-idempotency.md · comment 968756b5 · parent TSBC-1585 remains in_progress.

judgeDetail.rationale: Correctly names non-idempotent at-least-once handling, explicitly covers duplicate order, duplicate license email, and double-counted revenue, and fixes with event.id dedup key + uniqueness + skip side effects on conflict, though it doesn't explicitly bind the check and side effects in one transaction.
